# Data import

`import metallurgypy.data_io`

Import of tabular data (CSV, JSON, optional XLSX) into validated quantities.

## `BatchItem`

```python
class BatchItem(row_number: int, result: CalculationResult | None, error: str | None = None) -> None
```

## `ColumnMapping`

```python
class ColumnMapping(column: str, name: str, unit: str | None = None, kind: str = 'number', required: bool = True, minimum: float | None = None, maximum: float | None = None) -> None
```

How one file column becomes one named value (``kind='number'`` needs a ``unit``).

class RejectedRow(row_number: int, reasons: tuple[str, ...], raw: tuple[Any, ...]) -> None

## `Table`

```python
class Table(columns: tuple[str, ...], rows: tuple[tuple[Any, ...], ...], source: str = '', delimiter: str | None = None, decimal: str = '.') -> None
```

Raw table: header names and rows of raw cell values (str, int, float or None).

## `detect_column_types`

```python
detect_column_types(table: Table, *, threshold: float = 0.8) -> dict[str, str]
```

``'number'`` if at least ``threshold`` of the non-empty cells parse as numbers, else ``'text'``.

A few typos therefore do not turn a numeric column into text; the bad cells are
reported row by row when the data is imported.

## `guess_unit`

```python
guess_unit(header: str) -> str | None
```

Unit written at the end of a header, e.g. ``'Cu grade [%]'`` -> ``'%'`` (only if known).

## `import_table`

```python
import_table(table: Table, mappings: Sequence[ColumnMapping]) -> ImportReport
```

Validate every row against ``mappings``; unusable rows are reported, not dropped silently.

## `read_table`

```python
read_table(path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, delimiter: str | None = None, decimal: str | None = None, encoding: str = 'utf-8-sig', sheet: str | None = None) -> Table
```

Read ``.csv``/``.txt``/``.tsv``, ``.json`` or ``.xlsx`` (needs ``openpyxl``).

## `run_batch`

```python
run_batch(model: str | ModelSpec, rows: Sequence[ImportedRow], fixed: Mapping[str, Quantity] | None = None) -> tuple[BatchItem, ...]
```

Run one registered model on each imported row (``fixed`` supplies shared parameters).

A failing row gives an item with ``error`` set; the other rows still run.

## `write_rejected_csv`

```python
write_rejected_csv(path: str | os.PathLike[str], report: ImportReport, *, overwrite: bool = False) -> Path
```

Write the rejected rows and their reasons to a *new* file (the source is never touched).
